chunks: From him, from Abū Jaʿfar, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī al-Washshāʾ, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, who said:

I heard Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام say: “When a man dies among women, his wife washes him. If his wife is not with him, then the one among them who has the greatest right to him washes him, and she wraps a cloth around her hands.”

key_terms.أَوْلَاهُنَّ بِهِ: the one with the greatest right to him among them; the nearest or most entitled woman
key_terms.امْرَأَتُهُ: his wife; the spouse who has priority in washing him
key_terms.خِرْقَةً: a cloth; something wrapped around the hands during the washing
key_terms.غَسَّلَتْهُ: washed him; performed the ritual washing of the deceased
key_terms.مَاتَ: died; the occurrence of death that triggers the funeral rulings

ai.seo_question: Who may wash a deceased man if only women are present?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about washing a deceased man when only women are present. It states that his wife should perform the ghusl, and if she is absent, the woman most closely entitled to him may wash him while covering her hands with a cloth.
